item.title: [DE|Primary] Ö1 Journal um acht (Sun 19:21): Abendjournal um 18 (18.10.2026)
[EN|In-Depth] BBC Global News Podcast (Sun 22:00): The Global Story:Was World War Two worth it? Some US conservatives have doubts
item.description:
Originally published Sun 18 Oct 2026 22:00 IDT.

Since World War Two ended, most people living in the United States or Europe have generally upheld a consensus about its morality; that it was a just war fought against an evil Nazi regime, and the allies were right to fight it. But in a viral podcast debate with the British conservative Sir Jacob Rees-Mogg, Tucker Carlson seemed to disagree with that narrative, causing deep consternation within the wider conservative movement. The Global Story’s Tristan Redman speaks to BBC Newscast’s Adam Fleming about Sir Jacob Rees-Mogg and the strand of British conservatism he represents. We also hear from the Conservative politician and Times of London columnist Lord Daniel Finkelstein - whose parents were survivors of a Nazi concentration camps and a Russian gulag - about why he thinks one of America’s most influential right-wing voices is casting doubt on World War Two history.

For more from the Global Story please subscribe wherever you get your BBC podcasts.

He gestures with both arms outstretched to the side as he speaks into a mic. He wears a dark blue jacket, a blue and white gingham shirt and a dark blue tie with yellow, diagonal stripes.
